_readme: Events and Multimedia Production, Version 1.4: the page's words and its media configuration, section by section (src/pages/work/events-video.astro and src/components/events/). Copy follows John's Combined Build Brief and the V1.1, V1.2, V1.3 and V1.4 delta briefs (October 14, 2026) and the facts in his working log; no metric is published until it has been verified, and nothing here mentions an unannounced pilot, contract or Foundation discussions, investor diligence, data rooms or fundraising. Media slots name asset ids in src/data/assets.json: to replace a placeholder, drop the file in and approve its entry there; the layout never changes, because every slot already holds its final aspect ratio. Unapproved slots show a labeled placeholder in `npm run dev` only and nothing in a production build.

hero._hero: One editorial reel (V1.2), in place of V1.1's three programs and their control: the chapters below, in this order, each one video cut from the brief's ranges (assets.json has each chapter's ranges and edits), played through once and crossfaded (350ms) into the next, round and round, muted. The label at the top left of the frame reads the chapter's number and title, numbered in order among the chapters whose video is approved and present: the team interview's chapter is pending, so it is left out entirely (no placeholder) and the chapters after it carry the lower numbers until its video is added. `pos` places the crop of the wide cinematic frame on each video (object-position), chosen so the burned-in captions stay whole and clear of the rail, and heads stay in, at both of the frame's proportions (2.2:1, and 2.4:1 on shorter wide screens); `fitNarrow` is how the video fills the 16:9 frame on narrow screens.
hero.headline: From live experience to lasting momentum.
hero.copy: I turn live opportunities into complete marketing systems, from sponsorship and on-site production to content, distribution, and the relationships that continue after the room clears.

monitor._monitor: V1.4, the program monitor's few words: beside the label at the top left a steady tally dot (lit while the reel plays) and `program`, so it reads PROGRAM · 01 / LIVE PRESENTATION; `timecode` before the running counter at the top right (TC 00:00:04:22). On the smallest frames the counter steps aside first, then the word.

transition._transition: Replaces the run of show (V1.1): the five stages as one phrase, revealed word by word over about seven tenths of a screen of scrolling, held, then straight into the activation. On small screens it breaks into two lines after `break` words.

activation.headline: The work starts before anyone enters the room.
activation.copy: Before the doors open, I negotiate sponsorships and pricing, coordinate with event hosts, source and price merchandise, and work with design on screen animations and physical assets. I plan how those pieces come together on site and how the activation continues through content and distribution afterward.
activation._visual: An original 3D render of the activation (V1.1, replacing the schematic; since V1.3 a concept rendering combining the activation elements John plans and coordinates across events, tied to no one event or booth, as the paragraph and the caption say): an illustrative composite, not a photograph, made for this page in Blender (scripts/render/; the spatial and lighting reference is reference/events-video/booth-render.png, never published). The television and the projected wall play their loops while the frame is in view; reduced motion, a data-saving preference, a small screen or no JavaScript keep the render with both screens on their poster frames.
activation.caption: Concept rendering combining the activation elements I plan and coordinate across events.

deck._deck: 04 The Expanding Production Deck (V1.3, deployed from the V1.2 review checkpoint; V1.4 made it one vertical accordion at every width): the live presentation, the production room and the event film in one stack, every chapter's header always visible and one chapter open at a time (the live presentation to begin with), opened by a click, a tap or the keyboard; nothing advances by itself. An open chapter holds its media and its words side by side on wide screens (the media about 58% of the two columns), stacked on narrow ones: its headline, one line of context, up to three things John did, the outcome, one credit line, and its media, a muted preview (an approved loop of 8 to 15 seconds that plays only while it is shown and in view, with its own pause control) and the full film, which `watch` plays in place with sound and its controls. The production room opens on its setup photograph (setupFinal below).

chapters.label: Live presentation
chapters.headline: Build the session. Fill the room. Extend its life.
chapters.context: I organized and ran Bolt Liquidity’s presentation at Sui Summit, ETHDenver, in 2025 and 2026, from the speaking slot to the recording.
points: Booked the slot, helped shape the subject and promoted the session
Directed the deck and ran the setup and live slides
Captured it from multiple angles, then published it whole and in clips
chapters.outcome: Event-led relationships contribute to ongoing conversations and integrations with key partners.
chapters.credit: Organized, directed and captured by John Cowin · Speaker Max McKendry · Deck design Bob van der Meer

chapters.label: Production room
chapters.headline: A compact setup. A full content system.
chapters.context: At ETHDenver 2026 I booked a production room at the venue and built a studio from what was on hand.
points: Set up two cameras, a clip-on mic and the venue’s own light
Wrote about 20 questions and directed multiple takes
Chose the strongest takes and wrote the edit direction
chapters.outcome: Finished explainers, edited by Bob van der Meer from my takes and direction.
chapters.credit: Questions, direction, capture and edit briefs by John Cowin · On camera Max McKendry · Final edit Bob van der Meer

chapters.label: Event film
chapters.headline: If you cannot own the stage, create the moment everyone shares.
chapters.context: Bolt was not a sponsor at Sui Fest, TOKEN2049 Singapore, so the opportunity had to be made.
points: Interviewed established teams on camera, Bolt one voice among many
Tagged every team, giving each a reason to share it
chapters.outcome: Tens of thousands of impressions and hundreds of likes, shared by the teams themselves.
chapters.credit: Concept, interviews, coordination and distribution by John Cowin · With Cetus, Bluefin, 7K DeFi, NAVI & Astros, FlowX Finance, DoubleUp, Claynosaurz and Talus

setupFinal._setupFinal: V1.4: the production room's Setup and Final, restored inside its chapter of the deck. Two tabs in the media area: Setup, the default, shows the behind-the-scenes photograph with its caption beneath; Final crossfades, within the same stage, to the finished explainer (the chapter's muted preview with its pause control, and Watch full video with sound). The reader makes the switch; nothing changes by itself, the stage keeps its size, and with reduced motion the change is immediate. Never side by side. `label` names the two tabs for assistive technology.
setupFinal.label: Setup and final
setupFinal.caption: Two cameras, two tripods, a clip-on mic, a laptop, and the venue’s existing lighting.

conclusion._conclusion: V1.2: the conclusion and the former Amplify section (Every event opens a longer conversation.) in one closing: the static row of the five stages as a quiet callback (never animated a second time), the headline, one paragraph, then the way on to the next case study in order, Creator Campaigns (the collection wraps around), then Contact.
conclusion.headline: The room clears. The work keeps moving.
conclusion.copy: An event is only the starting point. I turn live moments into content, extend their reach through partner and ecosystem distribution, and carry that momentum into strategic relationships and new opportunities.
conclusion.nextLine: Next, see how I build creator partnerships into campaigns designed to travel.
